ux.purpose: Get a client to review the site, collect and resolve their comments, and prove what changed since they approved.
ux.task: Send this site to my client for the first time
ux.finding: Review is the only module with no rail button: its tab config carries no `zone`, and the zone-driven rail render therefore omits it. The reachable doors are the Site menu's 'Review' item, the topbar review pill, the topbar CTA when the next move is a review one, the ReviewBar's Compare link, and the History panel's 'Compare with current' — and every one of the last four exists only once a round already exists (REVIEW_PILL.none is null, ReviewBar returns null with no active round, the approval band only renders when approved). So the FIRST send has exactly one door, buried in an overflow menu, and it is not the one users look in. In the standalone demo at :5050 the same is true — the rail has no Review tab there either.
ux.evidence: tabsConfig.ts:231-244 — the review entry has section/pattern/shortcut/mode but no `zone`, with the comment 'No `zone` → the zone-driven rail render leaves it out'. SiteMenu.tsx:44-55 documents the same fact and :203 renders the one menu item. StudioHeader.tsx:136-142 REVIEW_PILL none -> null; ReviewBar.tsx:116 returns null unless PENDING/CHANGES_REQUESTED. SavesChrome.tsx:129-138 only renders under isApproved. Searched: 'review' in tabsConfig.ts, 'onOpenReview', 'UI_PANEL_OPEN', 'openLeftPanelToTab("review"'.
ux.fix: Give Review a rail seat, or put 'Send for review' on the primary surface where the intent forms (next to Publish). A feature whose only cold-start door is an overflow menu will read as unbuilt.

ux.purpose: Get a client to review the site, collect and resolve their comments, and prove what changed since they approved.
ux.task: Re-send the round from the review bar
ux.finding: The review bar's 'Re-send' calls the shell's resend with no client email. The shell only mints a review token when it is given one, so the new round ships with token: null — the client receives no working link, while the button reports success and the old link is superseded. This is the exact defect the Review panel's own code documents having fixed for itself by passing the round's invitedEmail; the bar was never given the same fix.
ux.evidence: ReviewBar.tsx:104-113 `await onResend()` — no argument; AquibraStudio.tsx:401-421 resendReview(clientEmail?) -> submitForReview(undefined, undefined, clientEmail, snapshotPages) with the comment at :410-417 spelling out the consequence. The corrected caller is ReviewTab.tsx:292-294 `onResend(round?.invitedEmail ?? undefined)` with its own comment at :288-291. Searched: 'onResend', 'resendReview', 'invitedEmail', 'submitForReview'.
ux.fix: One re-send path, owned by the panel, with the bar linking to it — not a second implementation of the same verb that drops the argument that makes it work.

ux.purpose: Get a client to review the site, collect and resolve their comments, and prove what changed since they approved.
ux.task: Re-send a round while comments are still open
ux.finding: The same destructive verb ships twice with different safety. In the panel, re-sending with open comments raises an inline confirm that says the client gets a NEW link and the old one stops working immediately. In the bar — which is on screen the entire time a round is live, directly under the topbar — the same button fires straight through with no confirm at all. The safer copy exists; the more prominent control does not use it.
ux.evidence: ReviewTab.tsx:842-855 onClick -> if (openComments.length > 0 && !round.revoked) setConfirmResend(true), confirm panel at :795-816 with the 'old one stops working immediately' sentence. ReviewBar.tsx:148-159 renders Re-send with only a `resending` disable. Searched: 'confirmResend', 'doResend', 'Re-send'.
ux.fix: Route the bar's button at the panel's confirm, or drop it. Two live affordances for the same irreversible action is exactly the condition the panel's own comment warns about.

ux.purpose: Get a client to review the site, collect and resolve their comments, and prove what changed since they approved.
ux.task: Compare the approved page against the current one
ux.finding: Compare renders two full web pages side by side inside a left-drawer panel whose default width is 280px — about 130px per pane once padding, borders and the gap are taken. The Compare screen also replaces the panel header entirely with a two-item toolbar, so while it is open there is no expand control, no close, and no help: the only control that could widen the panel to 700px has been removed from the screen that needs it most. The result is two unreadable thumbnails, a second toolbar stacked under the first, and a title ('Compare with approved') that the inner toolbar then does not repeat.
ux.evidence: ReviewTab.tsx:498-505 the compareOpen branch returns a Toolbar with a Back Button and a literal span, replacing the PanelHeader used by every other state (:333-341). ApprovedCompareView.tsx:146-185 the inner toolbar has no title; :261-275 the split stage renders two <Frame> iframes at flex-1. tokens.generated.css:129 --bk-size-drawer: 280px; LeftSidebar.tsx:586 isExpanded -> 700. Searched: 'compareOpen', 'PanelHeader', 'STAGE', '--bk-size-drawer'.
ux.fix: Compare is a full-surface job, not a drawer job — open it on the canvas surface (as Settings already does with mode: fullpage), or at minimum keep the expand control and open it pre-expanded. One header, not two.

ux.purpose: Get a client to review the site, collect and resolve their comments, and prove what changed since they approved.
ux.task: Decide what to do about the drift I just found
ux.finding: Compare is read-only and ends nowhere. It shows what changed since approval and offers no next move — no 'Re-send for approval', no 'Publish anyway', no way to mark a change as intended. There is also no conflict state at all: the panel has no notion of 'the client approved v3 while you were editing', so the two sides are always presented as simply different, never as competing.
ux.evidence: ApprovedCompareView.tsx:146-296 — the toolbar is mode buttons + spacer + count + page Select + refresh, and the body is frames or a change list; no action anywhere. ReviewTab.tsx:498-540 wraps it with a Back button and nothing else. Searched 'conflict', 'Conflict', 'CONFLICT' across sidebar/tabs/review and panels/version-history — zero occurrences; 'Review both' — zero occurrences in src/.
ux.fix: End Compare on a decision: 'Send these changes for approval' / 'Publish anyway' / 'Dismiss'. When both sides moved, say so and let the user choose which to keep.

ux.purpose: Get a client to review the site, collect and resolve their comments, and prove what changed since they approved.
ux.task: Look at the review as a viewer
ux.finding: The panel computes the user's role and uses it in exactly one place — the 'Send for review' control's disabled reason. Resolve, Reopen, Reattach, Revoke link / Withdraw request and Re-send for review are all rendered live and unexplained for a VIEWER, who will click them and get a server rejection with no chrome explaining why. The pattern the codebase already uses (a named disabled reason) exists two lines away.
ux.evidence: ReviewTab.tsx:146 `const isViewer = useEditorRole() === "VIEWER"` — grep for 'isViewer' in the file returns exactly three hits: :146, :479 and :885, both of the latter being SendForReview's disabledReason. resolveButton at :558-562, revoke at :899-907, re-send at :842-855 carry no role check. Searched: 'isViewer', 'useEditorRole', 'disabledReason', 'readOnlyReason'.
ux.fix: Apply the same named-reason treatment to every mutating control in the panel. A control that is live for someone who cannot use it is worse than one that is visibly shut.

ux.screen: Topbar pill / Review bar / Review panel
ux.purpose: Get a client to review the site, collect and resolve their comments, and prove what changed since they approved.
ux.finding: One state — sent, nothing back — is named three different ways on three surfaces the user sees at once. The topbar pill says 'In review' or 'Opened · no reply'. The bar directly beneath it says 'Sent — waiting on your client'. The panel below that says '<Reviewer> has not commented yet. You will be notified.' Nothing reconciles them, and 'Opened · no reply' is derived from a field ('openedAt') that the review status enum does not even have a value for, so the pill can claim the client opened the link while the bar and panel say only that it was sent.
ux.evidence: StudioHeader.tsx:136-142 REVIEW_PILL table incl. 'opened-not-acted': 'Opened · no reply'. ReviewBar.tsx:126-132 the three-way expression: count>0 -> 'N open', CHANGES_REQUESTED -> 'Changes requested — nothing left open', else 'Sent — waiting on your client'. ReviewTab.tsx:626-634 emptyBody. ReviewBar.tsx:46-49 records that the DB enum is PENDING|APPROVED|CHANGES_REQUESTED with no OPENED. Searched: 'opened-not-acted', 'waiting on your client', 'nothing left open', '0 open'.
ux.fix: One vocabulary, defined once and consumed by all three surfaces, with the pill as the short form of the sentence the bar prints. If 'opened' is a real distinction, it needs to appear in the panel too; if it is not, drop it.

ux.purpose: Get a client to review the site, collect and resolve their comments, and prove what changed since they approved.
ux.task: Decide whether to publish over an old approval
ux.finding: There are two independent answers to 'what changed since approval'. The publish gate computes its own page-level diff and lists page names with a bare 'edited / added / removed' — no visual, no detail, capped at six with 'and N more'. The Review panel's Compare computes a typed, itemised diff with side-by-side and overlay rendering. The gate is the moment the user actually has to decide, and it shows the weaker of the two and offers no door to the stronger one.
ux.evidence: StaleApprovalModal.tsx:38-50 its own diffPages(); :162-181 renders page-name rows; the footer offers 'Re-send for approval' / 'Publish anyway' and no Compare. ApprovedCompareView.tsx:113-116 uses compareApprovedToCurrent from @/shared/utils/html with five typed change kinds. Searched: 'diffPages', 'compareApprovedToCurrent', 'StaleApproval', 'Compare'.
ux.fix: One diff, one component. Put 'See what changed' in the gate and open the real Compare; delete the second implementation.

ux.purpose: Get a client to review the site, collect and resolve their comments, and prove what changed since they approved.
ux.finding: The panel groups comments by page and resolves them individually, but there is exactly one reply box, at the bottom, which posts against a page derived from the FIRST comment in the list. A user answering the third comment on a different page has no way to attach the reply to it — and the helper text says only 'Replies are internal notes on the thread', which does not tell them which thread.
ux.evidence: ReviewTab.tsx:242 `const activePage = round && comments[0]?.pageId ? comments[0].pageId : undefined`; :244-258 send() -> postReply(body, activePage); the composer at :793-812 is a single Textarea outside every group. Individual rows carry only Resolve/Reopen (:558-562) and Reattach (:700-710). Searched: 'postReply', 'activePage', 'CommentRow', 'actions='.
ux.fix: Reply per comment, inline on the row, the way the resolve action already is. One global box over a grouped list will attach answers to the wrong question.

ux.purpose: Get a client to review the site, collect and resolve their comments, and prove what changed since they approved.
ux.task: Go to the thing that changed
ux.finding: List mode names every change ('Added', 'Removed', 'Content', with a label and a detail line) and none of them is clickable. Having found that a section was removed from /pricing, the user has to leave Compare, switch page and find it by eye. The rows are plain divs.
ux.evidence: ApprovedCompareView.tsx:211-226 — each change renders as a <div className={LIST_ROW}> with spans; no onClick, no selection emit, and no import of the composer (the component's props are approvedPages/currentPages/onRefreshCurrent only, :39-45). Searched: 'onClick', 'selection.select', 'setActivePage', 'CompareChange'.
ux.fix: Make a change row a destination: click it to switch to that page and select the element. The comparison is only useful if it ends on the canvas.

ux.purpose: Get a client to review the site, collect and resolve their comments, and prove what changed since they approved.
ux.task: Check drift from the version history and get back to it
ux.finding: The approval band in History offers 'Compare with current', which does not open a comparison in History — it switches the whole left panel to the Review module and opens Compare there. Compare's only exit is 'Back', which lands the user in the Review panel's comment thread, a module they never asked for, with no route back to the version list they started from.
ux.evidence: SavesChrome.tsx:129-138 emits UI_PANEL_OPEN { panel: 'review', screen: 'compare' }; TabRouter.tsx:226-236 maps activeSubTab 'compare' to ReviewTab's initialCompare; ReviewTab.tsx:500-503 the Back button sets compareOpen false, returning to the review thread; the deep-link fires once (:526-532 compareRequested ref) so there is no return path. Searched: 'UI_PANEL_OPEN', 'initialCompare', 'openLeftPanelToTab', 'compareRequested'.
ux.fix: Either render the comparison inside History (it is the same component), or make Back return to where the user came from. Cross-module deep links need a return address.

ux.purpose: Get a client to review the site, collect and resolve their comments, and prove what changed since they approved.
ux.task: Look at what happened in an earlier round
ux.finding: Opening the round strip lists previous rounds as plain text lines — 'Round 2 · Changes requested · 14/08'. They are spans, not controls: there is no way to open a round, read its comments, or see what was sent. A user who came here to answer 'what did they ask for last time' gets a list of outcomes and stops.
ux.evidence: ReviewTab.tsx:757-790 — each row is a <span> with a testid; no onClick anywhere in the block. The docblock at :743-747 states the data limit: comments carry no round id, so an older round's comments are not retrievable. Searched: 'roundsOpen', 'review-round-', 'fetchRounds'.
ux.fix: Either make the strip honest about being a log (label it 'Round history' and stop it looking like a list of destinations), or carry the round id on comments so a round can be opened. Right now it reads as broken navigation.

ux.purpose: Get a client to review the site, collect and resolve their comments, and prove what changed since they approved.
ux.finding: 'Next ›' walks the open comments in a loop and never says where the user is. There is no '3 of 7', no marker that the walk has wrapped, and no way to go back one. On a round with a dozen comments the user cannot tell whether they have seen them all.
ux.evidence: ReviewBar.tsx:88-102 next() — `const i = cursor % open.length` then setCursor(i + 1); the only rendered count is the aggregate at :126-132. No 'Prev' control exists in the file. Searched: 'cursor', 'Next', 'Prev', 'openCommentCount'.
ux.fix: Print position ('3 of 7'), add a back step, and mark comments as visited so the walk has an end.
